citations.assessment: The checked Shabbat reads Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi in the canopy ruling and again in the cap ruling.
The checked Rosh has Rav Shisha in the cap ruling, differing from the label associated with it in the gloss.
The checked Rif reads Rav Shisha. The gloss gives Shishi.
In the cap parallel this witness has Rav Shisha. The preceding canopy ruling has Rav Sheshet. The reported Shila reading is edition-specific and not independently established.
The checked Beitzah has Rav Assi in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.
The checked Merubbeh parallel reads Rav Assi.
The checked Bekhorot parallel reads Rabbi Assi. Preserve the distinction from Rav Assi in Beitzah/Bava Kamma.
The checked text has Rav Ashi reporting Rabbi Yochanan about a different sacrificial ruling.
The checked chain gives Rav Yehudah bar Shila from Rav Ashi from Rabbi Elazar. Assi remains the gloss’s proposed reading.
Rav Yehoshua visits Rav Ashi and explains why he will not eat while observing a dream fast.
The closely parallel dream-fast story explicitly has Rav Assi.
The reported Western version reads Rav Ashi. Keep Assi as the gloss’s proposed correction.
The checked Bavli places Assi in parentheses. The Rif and Rosh have Rav Ashi.
Both checked works give Rav Ashi.
Rashi calls Mordekhai a pupil of Rav Ashi and invokes Sotah’s escort incident.
The Gittin gloss also reads Rav Ashi as teacher and in the Sotah quotation.
The checked Sotah has Mordekhai escorting Rav Ashi. Its parasang rule is for a teacher who is not the pupil’s principal teacher.
The checked Berakhot parallel has Mordekhai escorting Rav Shimi bar Ashi, with the route variants.
The Glick Ein Yaakov to Sotah agrees with Berakhot on Rav Shimi bar Ashi.
